router.name: router_decide
router.description: Decide one candidate by its eval id: accept it as work, ignore it, or stop one of the Tickets on its thread. Call it once per candidate. A refused decision comes back as an error that says why; correct the call and try again.

eval.description: The eval id on the candidate's first line.

title.description: accept: a short title for the work.

scope.description: accept: what the worker must do, in your words and complete on its own.

plan.description: accept: session (one worker, the default) or swarm (wide research and tournaments only).

agents.description: accept with plan swarm: how many agents.

goal_template.description: accept with plan swarm: the goal template it runs, one the prompt names. Omit it for the default.

environment.description: accept with plan session: the machine its run_code runs on, one your instructions name. Omit it for the default.

budget_microusd.description: accept: the Ticket's whole budget in microusd. Omit it for the default.

acknowledge.description: accept: the first reply, instead of the standard one. An empty string sends none.

rules.description: accept of inferred work: the proactive rules it matches.

ticket.description: stop: the id of the Ticket to stop.

router.name: router_read
router.description: Read one trigger, thread or ticket by id. The answer names its neighbours by id; follow them one hop at a time when a candidate needs more context.

kind.description: Which kind of id it is, when it could be more than one.

worker.name: worker_report
worker.description: Report on your ticket. progress: still working, nobody is told. waiting: your turn is over and nothing is outstanding. ready: the result, sent to whoever asked; it ends the ticket. blocked or failed: you need a person; say why. dropped: nothing to do; ends the ticket silently. A refused report comes back as an error that says why.

text.description: For ready, the complete result for the person who asked; otherwise what happened, briefly.

question.description: One concrete question for a person, when only a person can answer it.

worker.name: worker_handback
worker.description: Hand back a new message that reached your ticket but is not yours to handle: a request beyond your scope, other work, or a stop. The Router judges it; do not act on it yourself.

trigger.description: The trigger id of the message.

reason.description: One sentence: why it is not yours.

worker.name: run_code
worker.description: Run one bash command in an isolated, offline Linux sandbox. /work is your ticket's directory: the only writable path, kept between calls. Other paths the operator mounted are read-only. No network, broker socket, host home or credentials. Files are written into /work before the command. Returns bounded {exit_code,stdout,stderr,timed_out,duration_ms,truncated}. timeout_seconds is 1-300 (default 120). A command still running after a few seconds moves to the background and returns {job,status:"running",note}: use job_wait or job_stop on it, or end your turn and its result comes back as new input.

worker.name: job_start
worker.description: Start one bash command in the background, in run_code's sandbox with /work as its directory, and return {job,status} at once. Keep working or end your turn: when it ends after your turn, its result comes back to you as new input. Each byte of its output reaches you once, so write long output to a file in /work. A ticket holds a few jobs at a time.

timeout_s.description: Kill it after this many seconds. Default and most: the operator's job limit (30 minutes unless set).

worker.name: job_wait
worker.description: Wait up to wait_s for a job. Returns its end ({job,status,exit_code,stdout,stderr,...}), or {status:"running"} with what it printed since you last looked. It returns early when new input waits for you; end your turn to read it.

job.description: The job id from job_start or run_code.

wait_s.description: Seconds to wait; 0 only looks. Default 30.

worker.name: job_stop
worker.description: Kill a job and return its end with what it printed that you had not read.

worker.name: fetch_url
worker.description: Fetch one live http(s) URL through the broker; returns status, headers and bounded body. Your only network egress.
